### The Multi-Year Compute Crunch

From founders setting up AI servers next to their wine cellars, to the biggest companies rationing compute, everyone is scrambling. [...] Everyone is chasing compute, per the WSJ in ‘The Desperate Hunt for AI Computing Power Is Upending Silicon Valley’. Even at the top of the heap, budgeting compute across teams is a big challenge. Google lost one of its star AI researchers, Noam Shazeer, whom it paid $2.7 billion in 2024 to bring back, when he left for OpenAI after his team’s compute was cut. Renting Nvidia’s older H100 chips on a one-year contract costs about 60% more than a year ago, per SemiAnalysis. Cloud providers now want [...] Cheaper isn’t always cheaper. Researchers at Stanford, Carnegie Mellon, Berkeley and Microsoft Research tested more than 6,800 tasks and found that in 32% of cases, the lower-priced AI model ended up costing more. In one test, Google’s Gemini 3 Flash ran 952 steps, spent about $14, and failed; Gemini 3.1 Pro finished in 85 steps, for about $1. And the same model can use a different number of tokens each time it runs the same task. Google points customers to spending caps and flexible pricing.

highlights: # Anthropic revenue surges 45% to nearly $17B in third quarter as AI giant gears up for IPO. Anthropic’s third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, according to an investor who attended a pre-IPO meeting with Anthropic leadership in San Francisco on Wednesday. Revenue in the first quarter was $4.7 billion, and $11.6 billion in the second quarter, according to the person who attended the investor day meant to familiarize prospective Anthropic investors before its highly anticipated IPO. The IPO is expected to precede a public listing by rival OpenAI, making Anthropic an early test of investor appetite for heavily unprofitable AI developers pursuing massive scale. Founded by former OpenAI executives, Anthropic has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models. Anthropic has also sought to distinguish itself through its focus on AI safety, warning of the dangers posed by increasingly capable systems even as it competes in the race to develop and commercialize more powerful models.

latest.title: Google finally releases Gemini 4 Argon - The Verge
latest.summary: After months of trailing its rivals, Google says Argon competes with the industry’s best. After months sitting on the sidelines of the frontier AI race, Google has finally launched its long-awaited Ge...
highlights: After months of trailing its rivals, Google says Argon competes with the industry’s best. After months sitting on the sidelines of the frontier AI race, Google has finally launched its long-awaited Gemini 4 Argon model, claiming it can compete with the best the industry has to offer. The model is rolling out today to Google’s higher-tier Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and AI mode in Search, as well to Ultra subscribers on its agentic development platform Antigravity. The model is launching with an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, around a fifth the cost of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic’s Fable 5 models. Landing just a day after Meta announced its own frontier model, Muse Wonder Full, Argon is a reminder of how quickly the balance of power can shift in AI, and that the frontier is far from a two-horse race.
